newsitem.title: RUSSIA: IMF's Camdessus set for top-level Russia talks.
newsitem.headline: IMF's Camdessus set for top-level Russia talks.

text.p: The head of the International Monetary Fund, Michel Camdessus, arrives in Russia on Monday to start high-level talks on a new loan tranche, a senior government official said.
The official, an aide to First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais, said Camdessus would meet Chubais on Tuesday.

Camdessus is also due to meet President Boris Yeltsin, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov and Central Bank Chairman Sergei Dubinin during his four-day visit.

The IMF, whose regular monitoring mission was in Moscow last week to prepare for the visit, has delayed several tranches of its $10 billion three-year loan due to low Russian tax receipts and officials are working on a statement of intent for 1997.

Chubais, appointed earlier this month to breath new life into a moribund economic reform programme, said last week that the IMF loans were becoming less important for Russia, although were still a significant way to attract foreign investment.

Government sources said Camdessus was due to give a lecture at Moscow's prestigious Institute of Foreign Relations on Wednesday, followed by a news conference. A second news conference is planned for April 3, the day Camdessus leaves.
